body:
Global crypto markets shed ground on Monday as total market capitalization slipped to $2.7T, a decline of 2.85% over the prior 24 hours, even as most majors are showing modest hourly recoveries that suggest the selling pressure may be exhausting itself. Volume across the board came in at $74.5B, a respectable figure that indicates the move was orderly rather than panicked. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 71, down just 2 points from yesterday's 73, meaning the market is still firmly in Greed territory and has not meaningfully repriced its risk appetite despite the drawdown. BTC dominance at 59.1% and ETH dominance at 11.3% tell you the story clearly: capital is consolidating around the blue chips rather than rotating into speculative tail risk, which is a structurally healthy sign even if the headline number looks soft.

Bitcoin printed at $79,568, off 0.41% on the 24-hour but up 1.70% on the week, and the 1-hour tick of +0.30% hints at stabilization after whatever intraday pressure drove the session lower. Volume of $22.95B is solid without being exceptional, suggesting this is a digestion move rather than a conviction-driven flush. A CoinDesk headline today noting that Bitcoin blinks less than gold when Treasury yields move is worth filing away: it reinforces the narrative that BTC's macro correlation profile is shifting, and that institutional positioning may be increasingly treating it as a duration asset rather than a pure risk proxy. Watch $79,568 as the immediate pivot; a clean hold here with expanding hourly volume would set up a retest of the prior weekly high, while a break below would expose the market to a deeper consolidation and sharply test the conviction of late longs.

Ethereum at $2,506.7 is the relative bright spot among the large caps, up 0.37% on the day and 2.50% on the week, with $11.5B in volume indicating genuine participation. The real action today, however, is in the mid-cap layer. Chainlink is the session's standout, up 7.74% in 24 hours and 18.10% on the week to $13.28, with volume at $0.88B; no single headline explains it cleanly, but the DBS and Citi announcement completing the first weekend tokenized cross-border deposit on Swift via tokenized deposits is precisely the institutional DeFi infrastructure narrative that LINK bulls have been waiting to see validated. Uniswap at $7.12 has gained 1.46% today and an extraordinary 38.80% over 7 days, making it the week's dominant performer in the ZIMR tracking universe and one that deserves scrutiny for mean reversion risk. DOT gained 5.48% today to $1.025, building on a 23.30% weekly surge, and AVAX added 4.97% to reach $8.07 with an 11.90% weekly gain. On the other side, SOL is the most notable laggard at -0.98% to $105.64 despite a Solana protocol upgrade headline about tripling transaction size; the market is either unconvinced or already had the news priced in.

The macro backdrop is running hot with several competing inputs. Yen intervention meeting US inflation data this week — flagged in a Cointelegraph headline — is the single most consequential scheduled risk for risk assets broadly, and crypto will not be immune if the inflation print forces a repricing of Fed terminal rate expectations. The UK regulator weighing an easing of the financial prediction market ban adds a quiet regulatory tailwind for the sector in one of the world's key financial jurisdictions, while the Philippines signaling a freeze on payment operator registration and tighter VASP checks is a reminder that the global regulatory envelope remains uneven. The security note regarding a potential 2-key breach that could theoretically hand control of $91 billion in USDT to hackers, as reported by CoinDesk, is the kind of systemic risk disclosure that the market is currently choosing to ignore given the Greed reading of 71, but it sits in the background as a tail risk that could reprice quickly if sentiment turns.

Looking ahead, the dominant catalyst this week is the US inflation data print, which will determine whether crypto gets the rate-cut optionality narrative reinforced or faces a renewed headwind from yields. The Citi and DBS Swift tokenization story is worth monitoring for follow-on institutional announcements that could sustain the LINK and broader DeFi infrastructure bid. Any Tether response to the USDT security report will need to be watched closely; silence or a weak rebuttal would be the scenario most likely to rattle stablecoin confidence and compress risk appetite sharply. For BTC, a clean daily close above $79,568 on improving volume would be the signal to add exposure; a failure there that coincides with a hotter-than-expected CPI print would put the weekly gain of 1.70% at serious risk and open a conversation about whether the broader market has been pricing in rate cuts that may not materialize on the timeline the market assumes.
